name: Afigya Kwabre South
facts: * August 2012: The incumbent MP, the late Hon. Emmanuel Owusu-Ansah died on Friday 22 June 2012 after a short illness. The resultant by-election planned for 14 August 2012 was postponed following a court order.

name: Asante Akim North
facts: * September 2008: The late Hon. Kwadwo Baah Wiredu, NPP MP for Asante Akim North constituency died in Pretoria, South Africa on 24 September 2008 but no by-election was organised because it was less than 3 months to the December 2008 general elections

name: Asawase
facts: * April 2005: Hon. Alhaji Muntanka Mohammed Mubarak (of the NDC) won with a majority of 11,142 votes in a by-election held on 21st April 2005 replacing the late Dr Gibrine also of the NDC who had won the seat in December 2004 general elections with a majority of 4,474 votes.

name: Fomena
facts: * January 2007: Hon. Nana Abu Bonsra (of the NPP) won with a majority of 7,522 in a by-election organised on 23rd January 2007. This followed the death of Hon. Akwasi Afrifa (also of the NPP).

name: New Edubiase
facts: * September 1993: Hon. Theresa Joyce Baffoe of the NDC beat Samuel Amoah of the NPP by 5,766 votes during the first ever by-election held in the 4th Republic on 30th September, 1993. This follows the death of the incumbent MP Hon. Mary Eugenia Ghann also of the NDC.

name: Offinso South
facts: * October 2006: Owusu Achaw Duah ( of the NPP) won with a majority of 10,097 votes in a by-election held on 24th October 2006. He replaced Kwabena Sarfo also of the NPP, who passed away earlier.

name: Asunafo South
facts: * January 2009: Results for the Asutifi South constituency were deferred but confirmed later with Alhaji Collins Dauda of the NDC being sworn in as validly elected MP

name: Asutifi South
facts: * January 2001: Due to the death of NPP Parliamentary Candidate Philip Kofi Adjapong Amoah few days to the 2000 general elections, voting was postponed and later held on January 3, 2001. Cecilia Djan Amoah, the NPP replacement candidate and also the widow of the deceased, won the seat with a majority of 550.

name: Nkoranza North
facts: * March 2007: Major (rtd) Derek Oduro (of the NPP) won with a majority of 43,631 votes in a by-election held on 13th March, 2007 after the incumbent MP Hon. Eric Amoateng had vacated the seat while standing trial in the United States for drug trafficking.

name: Tano South
facts: * February 1995: On 7th February 1995, Nana Koduah Kwarteng (NDC) beat Kofi Akrowiah (PCP) to second place with a majority of 3,867 from a field of four candidates. This also follows the passing of the incumbent MP the late Hon. Samuel Amonoo Koto Asamoah.

name: Wenchi
facts: * January 1995: On 24th January, 1995, Hayford Osei Kwadwo (NDC) won from a field of four candidates with a majority of 3,144. He replaced the late MP Hon. Emmanuel Obeng Mensah also of the NDC.

name: Gomoa East
facts: * April 2003: Hon. Richmond Sam Quarm (of the NPP) won with a majority of 6,024 votes in the by-election held on 8th April, 2003 following the death of the late Emmanuel Acheampong (also of the NPP) in a road traffic accident on February 9, 2003.

name: Upper Denkyira East
facts: * June 2004: Hon. Benjamin Kofi Ayeh (of the NPP) won the seat from a field of three candidates with a majority of 20,899 votes in a by-election held on 29th June 2004 following the death of the incumbent Hon. Charles Omar Nyanor (also of the NPP)

name: Akwatia
facts: * 2009: Parliamentary elections in the Akwatia constituency had problems and were therefore deferred. The Supreme Court of Ghana ordered that the election be re-run at six (6) polling stations. Following this, the collated results made Hon. Kofi Asare of the NPP the duly elected MP for the constituency.

name: Atiwa East
facts: * August 2010: A by-election was held on 31st August 2010 following the death of the Late Hon. Kwasi Annoh Ankama of the NPP. He died during a trip to London. Hon. Kwesi Amoako Atta also of the NPP, won the seat with a vote of 20,282 (75%). This gave him a majority of 14,092 (52.1%).

name: Ablekuma Central
facts: * March 1999: On 26th March 1999, Hon. Victor Okuley Nortey retained the seat for the NPP in the by-election with a majority of 4,808, following the death of the incumbent MP Clement Samuel Crabbe

name: Odododiodioo
facts: * August 2005: Hon. Jonathan Nii Tackie Komey (of the NDC) retained the seat for his party with a majority of 8377 votes in a by-election held on 30th August 2005 to replace the late Samuel Nii Ayi Mankattah also of the NDC who had passed away earlier.

name: Bimbilla
facts: * March 2002: Hon. Dominc Aduna Bingab Nitiwul (of the NPP) won the by-election held on 14th March 2002 with a majority of 7621 votes, after�Dr. Mohamed Ibn Chambas (of the NDC)�had vacated the seat to take up his new job as the Executive Secretary of the�Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

name: Chereponi
facts: * September 2009: The late Hon. Doris Asibi Asiedu (of the NPP) died on 31 July 2009 after an illness. The EC organised a by-election on 29 September 2009 and Hon. Samuel Abdulai Jabanyite (of the NDC) was declared the winner and duly elected MP but later lost the seat back to the NPP in the 2012 elections.

name: Kumbungu
facts: * April 2013: As a result of Hon. Alhaji Mohammed Mumuni vacating his seat to take up the position of Secretary-General of African, Caribbean and Pacific States, a by-election was held on 30th April 2013 to elect his replacement. The seat was contested by the NDC, CPP and PPP. Amadu Moses Yahaya of the CPP, won with over 2,000 votes over his nearest competitor, Imoro Yakubu Kakpagu of the NDC. This becomes the first seat won by the CPP in the 6th Parliament of the 4th Republic.

name: Tamale Central
facts: * April 2006: Hon. Alhassan Inusah Fuseini (of the NDC) won with a majority of 17502 votes in a by-election held on 4th April 2006. This followed the resignation of Dr. Alhassan Wayo Seini, who resigned from the NDC to join the (NPP) but lost the resultant by-election.

name: Wulensi
facts: * March 2003: Hon.�Kofi Karim Wumbei (of the NPP), a teacher, won with a majority of 894 votes in the by-election held on 4th March, 2003�following the disqualification of the incumbent MP, Samuel Nyimakan of the NDC by the�Supreme Court of Ghana�on 15 January 2003. * July 2012: Following the death of the independent MP Late Hon. Alhaji Saani Iddi in early June,the EC set 31st July 2012 for a by-election following registration of candidates on 3 July and 4 July 2012. All four parties contesting contesting the by-election won a court injuction to postpone the by-election as they wanted the EC to use the new voters' register which was being finalised rather than the old register used in previous elections.

name: Bawku Central
facts: * July 2012: Adamu Dramani Sakande the then incumbent MP was jailed for 2 years by the Supreme Court of Ghana for forgery on 27 July 2012. This follows a case brought in the High court by Mr Sumaila Biebel, a cattle dealer in 2009 stating that Dramani did not qualify to be an MP as he held both a British and a Burkinab� passports.

name: Navrongo Central
facts: * July 1995: Following the death of the incumbent MP Godfred Abulu, the NDC lost one of its seats in Parliament to an Independent Candidate, John Setuni Achuliwor, who won the seat with a majority of 196 on 4th July 1995. * March 2003: Another by-election was held on 25th March 2003 and was won by Hon Joseph Kofi Adda (with 7,271 more votes) who retained the seat for the NPP following the death of Hon. John Setuni Achuliwor who died on 29th January 2003 after he was involved in a motor accident on 5th January 2003.

name: Jirapa
facts: * April 2009: Late Hon. Edward Salia of the NDC died after a period of illness necessitating a by-election which was held on 7th April 2009. Dr. Francis Bawaana Dakurah also of the NDC won the seat with a majority of 9,337 (59.0%) beating the NPP candidate and immediate past District Chief Executive for Jirapa, Justin Bayelah Dakurah to second place.

name: Lambussie-Karni
facts: *May 1995: On 26th May 1995, Alice Teni Boon (NDC) won the seat with a majority of 4,488 votes after the death of the incumbent Hon. Jacob Bawline Boon also of the NDC

name: Akatsi South
facts: * February 2013: Rt. Hon. Edward Korbly Doe Adjaho�of the�NDC�became the�Speaker of Parliament�on 7 January 2013�triggering a by-election, which was held on 5th February 2013. Hon.�Bernard Ahiafor of the NDC won by a majority of 3,767 votes (18.2%) to become the new MP.

name: Buem
facts: * February 2013: Following the sudden death of the Late Hon. Henry Ford Kamel of the NDC and then Volta Regional Minister on 25th December 2012, a by-election was held on 26th February 2013. This was won by Hon. Daniel Kosi Ashiaman of the NDC with a majority of 8,640 (78%) votes.

name: Keta
facts: * February 2007: Hon. Dan Kwashi Abodakpi as an incumbent MP was sentenced together with the late Victor Selormey, by the Accra Fast Track High Court to 10 years imprisonment on 5th February 2007 and was later granted a Presidential pardon by H.E Former President J. A. Kufuor on 24th May, 2008. No by-election was organised during his period of incaceration. He later returned to parliament on 10th June 2008 to finish his term.

name: Ketu South
facts: * 1996: In fulfilment of the Article 112 (6) of the 1992 Constitution, by-election could not be held because the incumbent MP, the late Wisdom Isidore Seyena-Susu passed away less than 3 months to the 1996 general elections

name: Amenfi West
facts: * April 2003: Mrs Agnes Sonful, teacher, 52, snatched the seat for the NPP with a majority of 4,121 votes in a by-election held on 24th April 2003 due to the resignation of Abraham Kofi Asante (of the NDC) on 26 March 2003. Mrs. Sonful subsequently lost the seat to Hon. Samuel Gyetuah of the NDC in the 2004 general elections.
